D018-D019_h001.question: It’s been over a month now since my husband passed away in that awful car accident, and things just haven't gotten any better. I keep replaying the whole thing in my head, especially that phone call I got at work. It just pops into my mind when I’m washing dishes, and I can almost hear the police officer’s voice. Sometimes, I catch myself just staring off into space, my mind just foggy and dazed – it’s like my brain won’t let me think clearly about anything else. I used to be so proud of keeping a spotless kitchen, but now, it just feels meaningless, no matter how good a job I do. I keep thinking, “If only that truck driver had been more careful!” It just…it feels like it was all his fault, you know? And I’m constantly on edge, like I’m waiting for something else bad to happen. Any sudden noise, like a dropped plate, makes me jump and flinch. I just want this constant fear to go away.
D018-D019_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D018-D019_h003.question:
It's been... well, over a month now since the accident. And it feels like I'm still stuck in that moment. Every time I see a car like the one that hit me, my heart races, and I feel this terrible fear wash over me. It’s like it’s happening all over again.

Honestly, I’ve lost all interest in styling. I used to love finding new clothes and putting looks together, but now it all just feels… pointless. My mind feels so cloudy, like I’m in a daze, and I can't think straight. Everything is just one big blur. Sometimes, if someone unexpected touches my arm, even accidentally, I jump out of my skin – it’s so unnerving.

I also can’t stop blaming the other driver. They were so careless, and if it wasn’t for them, none of this would have happened. The shock and horror of the crash haven’t faded at all; they’re just as vivid as they were the day it happened. It’s been weeks, and it’s still right there, fresh in my mind.

    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D018-D019_h004.question: "Well, doctor, it's been over a year now since the accident, since I lost my wife.
